entries.title: II Kings 3:3
segments: Cleaved unto the sins of Jeroboam; though he put away the image of Baal, he still continued to worship the golden calves.
Men may refuse to commit, or may break off some sins, and yet continue to practise others; but without a heart to hate and forsake all known sins, they must perish.

entries.title: II Kings 3:7
segments: When men engage in projects without acknowledging God or seeking his direction, especially when they join the wicked in the prosecution of their plans, they may expect to be brought into trouble, and will have special reason for gratitude if they escape destruction.

entries.title: II Kings 3:8
segments: The wilderness of Edom; south of the Dead sea.

entries.title: II Kings 3:11
segments:
Poured water; in washing one's hands, it was then customary for an attendant to do this. 
 
In times of danger it is always safest to go to God, and ask counsel of him.

entries.title: II Kings 3:14
segments:
Not look toward thee; not deign to notice him, or regard his request, because of his idolarty. 
 
From regard to his people, the Lord often bestows great blessings not only on them, but on others with whom they are connected; and the wicked may thus receive favors, which they would otherwise never obtain.

entries.title: II Kings 3:15
segments: A minstrel; one who could play on a musical instrument in praising God; and thus aid in preparing the mind of the prophet to be directed by him.

entries.title: II Kings 3:16
segments: God requires men in their troubles, not only to seek his help, but to show by their actions that they believe him and are willing to follow his directions; and unless they do this, they cannot reasonably expect that he will grant them relief.

entries.title: II Kings 3:18
segments: A light thing; only a small part of what God will do.

entries.title: II Kings 3:23
segments: Things often appear to the wicked to be very different from what they really are; and as they do not feel their need of divine guidance, and do not seek it, they have no security against fatal deception.

entries.title: II Kings 3:25
segments: Kir-haraseth; a stringly fortified place in the land of Moab; called also Kir-haresh.
The stones thereof; that is, the stones of which the wall was built.

entries.title: II Kings 3:26
segments: To break through; through the forces of the king of Edom, and so perhaps escape.

entries.title: II Kings 3:27
segments:
Offered him; as a sacrifice to his idols, hoping in that way to obtain their help. 
 
The devices of men to atone for their sins and obtain help from idols, are sanguinary and cruel.  The leave the heart wedded to its lusts, and are utterly vain.
